page.layout: One page of text in a single column; running head at top; a catchword-like fragment "Et" at the lower right; no margin notes.

p.i:
Spiritibus, mox deinde silens, similisque dolenti
Infuscat vocem, tacitisque immurmurat umbris.
Mox fractos inter gemitus, iterumque cadentes
Integrat, & pleno reuocat sua carmina cantu,
Prolixam intendens animos in vocibus auram,
Vnáque tot lituos tormentáque musica vincit
Garrula, natiuisque modis, & simplice voces.

Ergo age, sine, precor, nobis per frondea Iura
Confraga, sine, precor, lógos philomela per annos,
Et tibi perpetuum ver floreat, atráque nunquam
Tempestas nimbosa hyemis tua carmina turbet:
Qua nec ignauus coccyx, soboleméque tenellam
Nec turpis foueat buffo, dum cautibus absens
Indulges, fruticum sidens sub fronti bus atrus:
Tantus amor, cantúsque rapit te gloria tanta.

Ergo age, sine, precor, nobis per frondea Loza
Confraga, sine, precor, lógos philomela per annos.
Tu modo non tanto recolas tua carmina luctu,
Aut interrumpas dulces male grata querelas.

Huc quoties, ut te liceat spectare canentem,
(Verum audire sat est) venio, solusque sub umbra
Vel saceo, virides vel propter obambulo ripas,
Aut Loza, aut Anna liquido sua nomina Loza
Qui miscet, tacitus mecum mea carmina ludens
Dum meditor, veteréisque iuuat copellere musas
Paulisper flores & legens, herbásque potentes
Nunc has, nunc illas demiror, & omnia lustro
Sedulus, aut faciem, aut vires exploro latentes:
Sive aliquâ admirans describo in pulvere formâ.

page.notes: Page is a single text column; the right-hand edge is cut off, so line endings are partly lost. Marks such as s and f read as long s, rendered as s. Several words in the italic verse are uncertain and may be misread (e.g. "Qua nec ignauus", "tenellam", "Loza"). The final line "Ei" is partially visible at the lower right and may be a catchword; the page number is not printed.
